title: Zeal

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was bitachon, and your line: trust. Today, the trait that gets up and goes.

"And Abraham rose early in the morning." That line, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation, opens the morning Abraham sets out for the binding of Isaac. The rabbis noticed the timing. Nothing in the command told him when to go. He could have waited a day, or a week. He went at dawn. From one detail about the hour, the Talmud draws a rule that reaches every ordinary good thing a person means to do.
screen: `ABRAHAM ROSE EARLY.` → `NOBODY SAID WHEN.` → `ONE DETAIL, ONE RULE.`

segments.voice: Zerizut. Zeal: doing good promptly, not later. Turn it four ways. First, the rule. The Talmud, in tractate Pesachim, says the zealous are early for mitzvot, and it learns this from Abraham rising early. In Hebrew: zerizin makdimin l'mitzvot. Second, how later works. Later is a soft word. A thank-you note waits a day, then a week, then feels too late to send. A visit to someone who is sick waits until they're better. Zerizut notices that good things can spoil by waiting. Third, the deer. Pirkei Avot keeps a saying of Judah ben Tema: be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle, swift as a deer and strong as a lion, to do the will of your Father in heaven. Swift as a deer is zerizut: not frantic, just light, sure, already moving. Fourth, the measure. Mussar sets every trait at its right amount, and zeal has one too. It isn't rushing through a prayer, or hurrying a friend who needs time, or answering before you've listened. It's closing the gap between deciding to do a good thing and doing it. Beside yesterday's trust, it's a partner: trust lets go of the outcome, and zeal doesn't let go of the doing.
screen: `THE ZEALOUS ARE EARLY.` · `GOOD THINGS SPOIL BY WAITING.` · `SWIFT AS A DEER.` · `CLOSE THE GAP, DON'T RUSH.` · then, large: `AND ABRAHAM ROSE EARLY IN THE MORNING.`

segments.voice: Ask what good thing you've been meaning to do: a message to someone who's struggling, a thank-you, a small repair. If it fits in the next two minutes, a short text, a note, do it now; if not, take the first step, like opening the message or writing the name. If you pray, you can begin the way some Jews begin a mitzvah, with a blessing.
Zerizut. Zeal: closing the gap between meaning to do good and doing it. The zealous are early for mitzvot. Today's word.
Your line: promptly. A good thing done now can't spoil by waiting. See you at dawn.

howItsDone: Jewish law applies the principle that the zealous are early for mitzvot, for example by holding a baby boy's circumcision early in the day, and Mussar students practice zerizut by acting on a good intention as soon as it arises.
